MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r18.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd reports that Moses asked which daughter the father intended; the father chose the one who had summoned him, and Moses objected unless that reflected the father’s preference before the father agreed and married her to him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r18.anchor: فروى عبد الرحمن بن زيد أن موسى قال : فأيهما تريد أن تنكحني

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r19.claim: The phrase means working for eight years; “work” is omitted because the term implies it, and the work was herding sheep.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r19.anchor: عمل ثماني حجج فأسقط ذكر العمل

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r20.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r20.claim: One view makes the eight years the bride’s dower.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r21.claim: The other view treats the eight years as the father’s condition for the marriage, not as dower.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r21.anchor: الثاني : أنها شرط الأب في إنكاحها إياه وليس بصداق

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r22.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r22.claim: Ibn Abbas says eight years were obligatory for Moses and the additional two were voluntary; God completed his term and he fulfilled ten.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r22.anchor: قال ابن عباس كانت على نبي الله موسى ثماني حجج واجبة وكانت سنتان عدة منه فقضى الله عنه عدته فأتمها عشرا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r23.speaker: ابن إسحاق
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r23.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the father promised good companionship.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r23.anchor: من الصالحين في حسن الصحبة . قاله ابن إسحاق

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r24.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r24.claim: The other interpretation is that the father would prove true to what he had promised Moses.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r25.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r25.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam says the father granted Moses every lamb born with a color unlike its mother’s; God instructed Moses to put his staff in the water, after which all lambs were born unlike their mothers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r25.anchor: حكى يحيى بن سلام أنه جعل لموسى كل سخلة توضع على خلاف شبه أمها

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r26.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r26.claim: Another account says the father granted Moses every spotted lamb and all the lambs were born spotted.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r26.anchor: وقال غير يحيى : بل جعل له كل بلقاء فولدن كلهن بلقا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r31.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r31.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r31.claim: The Prophet says Moses hired himself out for the sake of his chastity and food; when asked which term he fulfilled, he answered that he fulfilled the better and more complete one.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p247/r31.anchor: فروي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( إن موسى أجر نفسه بعفة فرجه وطعمة بطنه

MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r8.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r8.speaker: جبريل
MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r8.claim: Abu Imran reports Gabriel's instruction that, if asked which term Moses completed, the Prophet should say the better and more honorable one; if asked which daughter he married, say the younger, named Safuriyya.
MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r8.anchor: قال جبريل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن سألوك أي الأجلين قضى موسى فقل أفضلهما وأكرمهما

MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r9.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r9.speaker: الحسين بن علي
MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r9.claim: Al-Husayn ibn Ali says Moses completed the longer of the two terms; the report gives his wife's name as Balaqis.
MUJAHID:v2p482#3/r9.anchor: عن مقسم أبي عبد الرحمن قال قلت للحسين بن علي أي الأجلين قضى موسى قال أكثرهما

MUJAHID:v2p485#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p485#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p485#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says Moses served ten years, then remained for another ten years.
MUJAHID:v2p485#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قال قضى ( 3 ) موسى عشر سنين ثم مكث بعد ذلك عشر سنين أخرى

MUQATIL:28:26-27/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:26-27/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:26-27/r3.claim: Shuayb offers to marry one of his two daughters to Moses.
MUQATIL:28:26-27/r3.anchor: إني أريد أن أنكحك إحدى ابنتي } يعني أن أزواجك إحد ابنتي { هاتين على أن تأجرني

MUQATIL:28:26-27/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:26-27/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:26-27/r4.claim: Moses is to work for Shuayb for eight years.
MUQATIL:28:26-27/r4.anchor: هاتين على أن تأجرني } نفسك { ثماني حجج فإن أتممت عشرا } يعنى عشر سنين،

MUQATIL:28:26-27/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:26-27/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:26-27/r5.claim: Completing ten years is voluntary on Moses's part.
MUQATIL:28:26-27/r5.anchor: فإن أتممت عشرا } يعنى عشر سنين، { فمن عندك

MUQATIL:28:26-27/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:26-27/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:26-27/r6.claim: Shuayb says he does not want to burden Moses with the additional two years.
MUQATIL:28:26-27/r6.anchor: ومآ أريد أن أشق عليك } فى العشر

MUQATIL:28:26-27/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:26-27/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:26-27/r7.claim: Here ṣāliḥīn means gentle or kind.
MUQATIL:28:26-27/r7.anchor: يعني وارفق بهم، في سورة الأعراف.

MUQATIL:28:26-27/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:26-27/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:26-27/r8.claim: Muqatil links this sense of kindness to Moses's instruction to Aaron, interpreted as being gentle with the people.
MUQATIL:28:26-27/r8.anchor: كقول موسى لأخيه هارون: اخلفني في قومي وأصلح

NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r1.claim: Ankihaka means I give you in marriage.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r1.anchor: ﴿ قال إني أريد أن أنكحك ﴾ أزوجك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r2.claim: These two implies he had other daughters; this is a proposal, not a contract, since a completed marriage would say I have married you.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r2.anchor: قوله هاتين يدل على أنه كان له غيرهما وهذه مواعدة منه ولم يكن ذلك عقد نكاح إذ لو كان عقد لقال قد أنكحتك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r3.claim: The condition is that Moses work as a hired laborer for the father.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r4.claim: The eight hijaj are a duration; hijja means year and hijaj is its plural.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r5.claim: Marriage in exchange for tending sheep is unanimously permissible as part of marital responsibility, unlike marriage conditioned on service.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r5.anchor: والتزوج على رعي الغنم جائز بالاجماع لأنه من باب القيام بأمر الزوجية فلا مناقصة بخلاف التزوج على الخدمة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r6.claim: Ten years would be voluntary extra work, not an obligation; if Moses chose it, it was his generosity.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r6.anchor: فذلك تفضل منك ليس بواجب عليك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r7.claim: The father does not want hardship by requiring the longer term; a weighty matter feels as though it splits a person between ability and inability.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r7.anchor: بالزام أتم الأجلين وحقيقة قولهم شققت عليه وشق عليه الأمر أن الأمر إذا تعاظمك فكأنه شق عليك ظنك باثنين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r8.claim: Righteousness can mean good treatment and keeping promises, or righteousness generally, which includes these.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r8.anchor: في حسن المعاملة والوفاء بالعهد ويجوز أن يراد الصلاح على العموم ويدخل تحته حسن المعاملة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r9.claim: The qualification relies on God's enabling help: the speaker acts only if God wills.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p233#4/r9.anchor: والمراد باشتراطه مشيئة الله فيما وعد من الصلاح الاتكال على توفيقه فيه ومعونته لأنه إن شاء فعل وإن لم يشأ لم يفعل

QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r9.claim: A guardian’s offering his daughter to a worthy man is an established good practice, followed by Umar offering Hafsa and a woman offering herself to the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r9.anchor: فيه عرض الولي ابنته على الرجل وهذه سنة قائمة عرض صالح مدين ابنته على صالح بني إسرائيل،

QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r10.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r10.claim: Ibn Umar reports Umar’s offer of Hafsa to Uthman after she became widowed; al-Bukhari alone transmits this report.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r10.anchor: قال ابن عمر: لما تأيمت حفصة قال عمر لعثمان: إن شئت أنكحك حفصة بنت عمر الحديث انفرد بإخراجه البخاري.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r11.claim: The verse indicates that marriage is contracted by the guardian and the woman has no independent role; this is the position of the jurists of the major centers.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r11.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دليل على أن النكاح إلى الولي لا حظ للمرأة فيه لأن صالح مدين تولاه، وبه قال فقهاء الأمصار.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r12.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r12.claim: Abu Hanifa disagrees with the guardian-centered rule.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r12.anchor: وخالف في ذلك أبو حنيفة. وقد مضى.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r13.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r13.claim: Malik holds that a father may marry off his adult virgin daughter without prior consultation; al-Qurtubi calls his argument from this verse strong.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r13.anchor: هذه الآية تدل على أن للأب أن يزوج ابنته البكر البالغ من غير استئمار، وبه قال مالك واحتج بهذه الآية، وهو ظاهر قوي في الباب،

QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r14.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r14.claim: Al-Shafii and many scholars share Malik’s position about a father marrying his adult virgin daughter without prior consultation.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r14.anchor: وبقول مالك في هذه المسألة قال الشافعي وكثير من العلماء.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r15.claim: Al-Qurtubi says Malik’s argument from the verse shows reliance on Israelite reports, as noted earlier.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:25-27/r15.anchor: واحتجاجه بها يدل على أنه كان يعول على الإسرائيليات كما تقدم.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r1.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r1.claim: Abu Hanifa says an adult woman may only be married with her consent; a minor may be married without consent because she cannot consent, with no disagreement on that point.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r1.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: إذا بلغت الصغيرة فلا يزوجها أحد إلا برضاها لأنها بلغت حد التكليف فأما إذا كانت صغيرة

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r2.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r2.claim: Al-Shafii’s followers infer that marriage requires wording of tazwij or inkah; Rabiʿa, Abu Thawr, Abu Ubayd, Dawud, and a report from Malik agree.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r2.anchor: استدل أصحاب الشافعي بقوله: { إني أريد أن أنكحك } على أن النكاح موقوف على لفظ التزويج والإنكاح.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r3.speaker: ربيعة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r3.claim: Rabiʿa, Abu Thawr, Abu Ubayd, Dawud, and a differing report from Malik support the restricted marriage wording.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r3.anchor: وبه قال ربيعة وأبو ثور وأبو عبيد وداود ومالك على اختلاف عنه.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r4.claim: The well-known Maliki position is that marriage is valid with any wording.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r4.anchor: وقال علماؤنا في المشهور: ينعقد النكاح بكل لفظ.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r5.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the verse does not prove al-Shafii’s rule because it is an earlier law, which the school generally does not treat as binding proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r5.anchor: لا حجة لهم في الآية لأنه شرع من قبلنا وهم لا يرونه حجة في شيء في المشهور عندهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r6.claim: Abu Hanifa, his associates, al-Thawri, and al-Hasan ibn Hayy allow marriage by a gift or other permanent transfer formula before witnesses, by analogy with divorce wording.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r6.anchor: وأما أبو حنيفة وأصحابه والثوري والحسن بن حي فقالوا: ينعقد النكاح بلفظ الهبة وغيره إذا كان قد أشهد عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r7.speaker: ابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r7.claim: Ibn al-Qasim says he knows no statement from Malik on a father gifting a daughter while intending marriage, but considers it valid like a sale.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r7.anchor: وتابعهم ابن القاسم فقال: إن وهب ابنته وهو يريد إنكاحها فلا أحفظ عن مالك فيه شيئا، وهو عندي جائز كالبيع.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r8.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r8.claim: Abu Umar says marriage cannot be contracted by a gift formula: explicit wording is needed for witnesses, marriage cannot be analogized to divorce, and ‘I permit’ and ‘I make lawful’ are insufficient too.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r8.anchor: قال أبو عمر: الصحيح أنه لا ينعقد نكاح بلفظ الهبة، كما لا ينعقد بلفظ النكاح هبة شيء من الأموال.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r9.claim: The report that spouses are made lawful by God’s word refers to the Quran, which uses marriage formulas rather than a gift formula; allowing the latter would erase a prophetic privilege.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r9.anchor: يعني القرآن، وليس في القرآن عقد النكاح بلفظ الهبة، وإنما فيه التزويج والنكاح،

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r10.claim: Offering one of two unnamed daughters is a proposal, not a contract: marriage cannot leave the spouse uncertain or contain an option.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r10.anchor: يدل على أنه عرض لا عقد لأنه لو كان عقدا لعين المعقود عليها له

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r11.speaker: مكي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r11.claim: Makki lists unusual features: the bride was unnamed, the term’s start unstated, the dowry service, and entry before payment.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r11.anchor: قال مكي: في هذه الآية خصائص في النكاح منها أنه لم يعين الزوجة ولا حد أول الأمد، وجعل المهر إجارة، ودخل ولم ينقد شيئا.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r12.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the daughter’s identity was probably settled in later negotiations: the proposal was initially general and specified afterward.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r12.anchor: أما التعيين فيشبه أنه كان في ثاني حال المراوضة، وإنما عرض الأمر مجملا، وعين بعد ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r13.speaker: أبو ذر
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r13.claim: A report attributed to Abu Dharr identifies Safura as the younger daughter and introduces the Prophet’s saying about which daughter Moses married.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27/r13.anchor: وقد قيل: إنه زوجه صفوريا وهي الصغرى. يروى عن أبي ذر قال: قال لي رسول الله

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r1.claim: The quotation introduced as Abu Dharr’s report from the Prophet says Moses fulfilled the better and fuller term and married the younger daughter, who came behind him and recommended hiring him.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r1.anchor: إن سئلت أي الأجلين قضى موسى فقل خيرهما وأوفاهما وإن سئلت أي المرأتين تزوج فقل الصغرى وهي التي جاءت خلفه

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r2.claim: One explanation for marrying the younger daughter is that Moses might favor her after seeing and accompanying her; offering the elder could have hidden his preference. Other explanations are possible.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r2.anchor: فلو عرض عليه الكبرى ربما أظهر له الاختيار وهو يضمر غيره.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r3.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r3.claim: Al-Qushayri relates a different report in which Moses married the elder daughter.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r3.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار أنه تزوج بالكبرى حكاه القشيري.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r4.claim: The verse does not imply that the service term’s starting point was omitted: the parties may have specified it in negotiation, otherwise it began at the contract.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r4.anchor: وأما ذكر أول المدة فليس في الآية ما يقتضي إسقاطه بل هو مسكوت عنه فإما رسماه، وإلا فهو من أول وقت العقد.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r5.claim: The verse plainly shows marriage in return for service, an arrangement recognized in Islamic law; a Prophetic report also allows Quran teaching as a marriage gift.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r5.anchor: وأما النكاح بالإجارة فظاهر من الآية، وهو أمر قد قرره شرعنا، وجرى في حديث الذي لم يكن عنده إلا شيء من القرآن

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r6.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r6.claim: In the report cited by the jurists, the Prophet asks what Quran the man knows; when he names al-Baqara and the next sura, the Prophet says to teach her twenty verses and she is his wife.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r6.anchor: فقال له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r7.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r7.claim: Malik disliked making service the marriage payment, while Ibn al-Qasim prohibited it.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r7.anchor: واختلف العلماء في هذه المسألة على ثلاثة أقوال: فكرهه مالك، ومنعه ابن القاسم،

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r8.speaker: ابن حبيب
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r8.claim: Ibn Habib, al-Shafii, and his associates permit service by a free person as dowry, such as sewing, building, or teaching Quran.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r8.anchor: وأجازه ابن حبيب وهو قول الشافعي وأصحابه قالوا: يجوز أن تكون منفعة الحر صداقا كالخياطة والبناء وتعليم القرآن.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r9.claim: Abu Hanifa rejects a man’s own service as dowry but permits a servant’s labor or lodging in his house because these are property.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r9.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: لا يصح وجوز أن يتزوجها بأن يخدمها عبده سنة، أو يسكنها داره سنة لأن العبد والدار مال،

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r10.speaker: أبو الحسن الكرخي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r10.claim: Al-Karkhi allows contracting marriage in the form of hire because Quran 4:24 calls the marriage payment wages.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r10.anchor: وقال أبو الحسن الكرخي: إن عقد النكاح بلفظ الإجارة جائز لقوله تعالى: فآتوهن أجورهن

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r11.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r11.claim: Abu Bakr al-Razi rejects this because hire is time-limited whereas marriage is permanent, so the contracts conflict.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r11.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الرازي: لا يصح لأن الإجارة عقد مؤقت، وعقد النكاح مؤبد، فهما متنافيان.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r12.speaker: ابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r12.claim: Ibn al-Qasim says the contract is dissolved before consummation but stands after; Asbagh reports disagreement if some payment was advanced and says an abandoned contract proceeds under the Madyan precedent.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r12.anchor: وقال ابن القاسم: ينفسخ قبل البناء ويثبت بعده. وقال أصبغ: إن نقد معه شيئا ففيه اختلاف،

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r13.speaker: ابن خويزمنداد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r13.claim: Ibn Khuwayz Mindad says the verse validates marriage for service, though using service as dowry is disliked and monetary payment preferable, citing Quran 4:24.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28/r13.anchor: قال ابن خويزمنداد. تضمنت هذه الآية النكاح على الإجارة والعقد صحيح، ويكره أن تجعل الإجارة مهرا

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r4.speaker: أبو زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r4.claim: The Abu Zayd collection gives the view that joining hire and marriage is initially disliked but stands if done.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r4.anchor: قال في ثمانية أبي زيد: يكره ابتداء فإن وقع مضى.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r5.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r5.claim: The well-known view of Malik and Ibn al-Qasim disallows combining hire and marriage and rescinds it before or after consummation because the contracts have different purposes.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r5.anchor: قال مالك وابن القاسم في المشهور: لا يجوز ويفسخ قبل الدخول وبعده لاختلاف مقاصدهما كسائر العقود المتباينة.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r6.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Arabi prefers permission from Ashhab and Asbagh, supported by the verse and Malik’s comparison of marriage to sale.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r6.anchor: أجازه أشهب وأصبغ. قال ابن العربي: وهذا هو الصحيح وعليه تدل الآية وقد قال مالك النكاح أشبه شيء بالبيوع،

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r7.speaker: المزني
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r7.claim: Al-Muzani cites a poet’s line about benefit and piety as an example of permissible poetry whose teaching may serve as a dowry.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#2/r7.anchor: قال المزني: وذلك مثل قول الشاعر: يقول العبد فائدتي ومالي وتقوى الله أفضل ما استفادا

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r1.claim: Teaching poetry containing insults or obscenity as dowry is invalid, like making wine or pork the dowry.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r1.anchor: وإن أصدقها تعليم شعر فيه هجو أو فحش كان كما لو أصدقها خمرا أو خنزيرا.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r2.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r2.claim: Malik permits unspecified service based on custom, so the agreement need not list tasks; the story’s general wording supports this.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r2.anchor: قال مالك إنه جائز ويحمل على العرف، فلا يحتاج في التسمية إلى الخدمة، وهو ظاهر قصة موسى،

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r3.claim: Abu Hanifa and al-Shafii reject unspecified service unless its tasks are named because it is indeterminate.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة والشافعي: لا يجوز حتى يسمى لأنه مجهول.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r4.speaker: البخاري
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r4.claim: Al-Bukhari titles a chapter about hiring a worker for a specified term without naming work, citing this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r4.anchor: وقد ترجم البخاري: «باب من استأجر أجيرا فبين له الأجل ولم يبين له العمل» لقوله تعالى: { على أن تأجرني ثماني حجج }.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r5.speaker: المهلب
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r5.claim: Al-Muhallab says the work was understood by custom as herding, farming, and similar rural labor; only an unknown term and unfamiliar work are invalid.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r5.anchor: قال المهلب: ليس كما ترجم لأن العمل عندهم كان معلوما من سقي وحرث ورعي وما شاكل أعمال البادية

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r6.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says commentators report sheep herding, without a sound transmission; Shuayb’s known occupation could itself specify the service.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وقد ذكر أهل التفسير أنه عين له رعية الغنم، ولم يرو من طريق صحيحة،

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r7.claim: Scholars agree a shepherd may be hired for known months, known wages, and a counted flock; details differ for identified animals.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r7.anchor: أجمع العلماء على أنه جائز أن يستأجر الراعي شهورا معلومة، بأجرة معلومة، لرعاية غنم معدودة

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r8.speaker: ابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r8.claim: Ibn al-Qasim says hiring for a specified flock is invalid unless replacements are stipulated if animals die; al-Qurtubi calls this very weak and notes Shuayb required no replacements.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن القاسم: لا يجوز حتى يشترط الخلف إن ماتت، وهي رواية ضعيفة جدا وقد استأجر صالح مدين موسى على غنمه

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r9.claim: Maliki scholars permit hiring for an unspecified flock by custom and the shepherd’s capacity; Abu Hanifa and al-Shafii reject it as indeterminate.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r9.anchor: وإن كانت مطلقة غير مسماة ولا معينة جازت عند علمائنا. وقال أبو حنيفة والشافعي: لا تجوز لجهالتها

QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r10.claim: Some Maliki scholars require the employer to know the shepherd’s capacity; al-Qurtubi approves, noting Shuayb saw Moses lift the stone.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:27#2/r10.anchor: وزاد بعض علمائنا أنه لا يجوز حتى يعلم المستأجر قدر قوته، وهو صحيح فإن صالح مدين علم قدر قوة موسى برفع الحجر.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r8.claim: The wage Moses received is not specified, but Yahya ibn Salam and other accounts describe payment through lamb offspring.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r8.anchor: لم ينقل ما كانت أجرة موسى عليه السلام ولكن روى يحيى بن سلام

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r9.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r9.claim: Yahya ibn Salam says Shuayb gave Moses every lamb born a different color from its mother; God instructed Moses to place his staff among the flock, producing such offspring.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r9.anchor: أن صالح مدين جعل لموسى كل سخلة توضع خلاف لون أمها، فأوحى الله إلى موسى أن ألق عصاك بينهن يلدن خلاف شبههن كلهن.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r10.speaker: غير يحيى
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r10.claim: Another account says Moses received every spotted lamb born, and all the lambs were spotted.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r10.anchor: وقال غير يحيى: بل جعل له كل بلقاء تولد له، فولدن له كلهن بلقا.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r11.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r11.claim: Al-Qushayri reports Moses repeatedly selected Adam’s inherited staff; it killed a dragon threatening the flock, and two-colored lambs miraculously became Moses’s reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#3/r11.anchor: وذكر القشيري أن شعيبا لما استأجر موسى قال له: ادخل بيت كذا وخذ عصا من العصي التي في البيت،

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r1.speaker: عيينة بن حصن
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r1.claim: Uyayna ibn Hisn reports the Prophet saying Moses hired himself for food to fill his belly and chastity for his private parts.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r1.anchor: وروى عيينة بن حصن أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r2.speaker: الهروي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r2.claim: Al-Harawi explains the reward as lamb offspring unlike their mothers, excluding sheep with several specified traits.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r2.anchor: فقال له شعيب لك منها يعني من نتاج غنمه ما جاءت به قالب لون ليس فيها عزوز ولا فشوش ولا كموش ولا ضبوب

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r3.speaker: الهروي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r3.claim: Al-Harawi defines azuz as a low-milking sheep, relating it to hard ground and noting the verb taʿazzazat.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r3.anchor: قال الهروي: العزوز البكيئة مأخوذ من العزاز وهي الأرض الصلبة، وقد تعززت الشاة.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r4.speaker: الهروي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r4.claim: Al-Harawi defines fashush sheep as those whose milk flows without milking due to a broad passage; he gives synonyms, an idiom for venting anger, and a hadith image of Satan blowing between a person’s buttocks.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r4.anchor: والفشوش التي ينفش لبنها من غير حلب وذلك لسعة الإحليل، ومثله الفتوح والثرور. ومن أمثالهم: لأفشنك فش الوطب

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r5.speaker: الهروي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r5.claim: Al-Harawi defines kumush or kumaysha as a small, contracted udder and says kushud is similar; he explains the phrase kamish al-izar.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r5.anchor: والكموش: الصغيرة الضرع، وهي الكميشة أيضا سميت بذلك لانكماش ضرعها وهو تقلصه ومنه يقال: رجل كميش الإزار.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r6.speaker: الهروي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r6.claim: Al-Harawi defines dabub as a narrow milk opening and dab as milking with strong pressure.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r6.anchor: والضبوب الضيقة ثقب الإحليل. والضب الحلب بشدة العصر.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r7.speaker: الهروي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r7.claim: Al-Harawi describes thaʿul as a sheep with an extra teat and explains thaʿl as an extra tooth and a narrow milk passage.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r7.anchor: والثعول الشاة التي لها زيادة حلمة وهي الثعل. والثعل زيادة السن، وتلك الزيادة هي الراءول. ورجل أثعل.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r8.speaker: الهروي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r8.claim: Al-Harawi defines qaalib lawn as offspring whose colors differ from their mothers.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r8.anchor: قال الهروي: وتفسير قالب لون في الحديث أنها جاءت على غير ألوان أمهاتها.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r9.claim: Hiring for unknown payment is invalid because the number and survival of lambs are uncertain, even in lands where births are predictable.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r9.anchor: الإجارة بالعوض المجهول لا تجوز فإن ولادة الغنم غير معلومة،

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r10.claim: The Prophet prohibited uncertainty and sale of unborn offspring in wombs or male animals’ loins; madamin and malaqih refer to these.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r10.anchor: لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نهى عن الغرر، ونهى عن المضامين والملاقيح. والمضامين ما في بطون الإناث، والملاقيح ما في أصلاب الفحول

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r11.speaker: راشد بن معمر
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r11.claim: Rashid ibn Muammar permits hiring for a flock in exchange for one-third or one-quarter of its offspring.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r11.anchor: على أن راشد بن معمر أجاز الإجارة على الغنم بالثلث والربع.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r12.speaker: ابن سيرين
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r12.claim: Ibn Sirin and Ata permit weaving a garment for a share of it, and Ahmad agrees.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r12.anchor: وقال ابن سيرين وعطاء: ينسج الثوب بنصيب منه وبه قال أحمد.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r13.claim: Marriage compatibility is legally considered, though scholars differ whether it concerns religion, wealth, lineage, or only some of these.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r13.anchor: الكفاءة في النكاح معتبرة واختلف العلماء هل في الدين والمال والحسب، أو في بعض ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r14.claim: Al-Qurtubi considers it valid for non-Arab clients to marry Arab and Qurayshi women.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:23-28#4/r14.anchor: والصحيح جواز نكاح الموالي للعربيات والقرشيات لقوله تعالى:

QASHANI:28:26-27/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:26-27/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:26-27/r7.claim: Giving one daughter in marriage means bringing her under the heart's command so she receives holy light and unveiling knowledge without veiling it.
QASHANI:28:26-27/r7.anchor: قال إني أريد أن أنكحك إحدى ابنتي هاتين

QASHANI:28:26-27/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:26-27/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:26-27/r8.claim: Eight years of service signify striving through eight stages: annihilation through the seven divine attributes, ending in intimate speech; a stage of witnessing completes the sought arrival.
QASHANI:28:26-27/r8.anchor: هي أطوار الصفات السبعة الإلهية بالفناء عن صفاته في صفات الله التي آخرها مقام المكالمة

QASHANI:28:27-28/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:27-28/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:27-28/r1.claim: Completing ten signifies two further stages, annihilation in the Essence and subsistence afterward; this depends on one's aptitude and the ten perfections Abraham completed before being made a leader.
QASHANI:28:27-28/r1.anchor: هما الفناء في الذات والبقاء بعده بالتحقق

RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r1.claim: The offer names one of two daughters without specifying which; at the marriage itself the bride becomes definite.
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r1.anchor: فلا شبهة في أن هذا اللفظ ، وإن كان على الترديد لكنه عند التزويج عين

RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r2.claim: The contract was concluded for the shorter term of eight years, making the extra two years a voluntary gift.
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r2.anchor: ولا شبهة في أن العقد وقع على أقل الأجلين ، فكانت الزيادة كالتبرع

RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r3.speaker: الفقهاء
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r3.claim: Jurists may cite the passage to show that labor can serve as a marriage dower just as money can.
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r3.anchor: والفقهاء ربما استدلوا به على أن العمل قد يكون مهرا كالمال

RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r4.speaker: الفقهاء
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r4.claim: Jurists may also cite it for the permissibility of adding an increase to the agreed consideration.
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r4.anchor: وعلى أن إلحاق الزيادة بالثمن والمثمن جائز ، ولكنه شرع من قبلنا فلا يلزمنا

RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r5.claim: These inferences concern a prior religious law and therefore do not bind Muslims as rulings.
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r5.anchor: ولكنه شرع من قبلنا فلا يلزمنا

RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r6.claim: That earlier law permitted a guardian to stipulate a benefit for himself in the marriage arrangement.
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r6.anchor: ويدل على أنه قد كان جائزا في تلك الشريعة أن يشرط للولي منفعة

RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r7.claim: That earlier law allowed marriage without a separate consideration owed to the woman.
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r7.anchor: وعلى أنه كان جائزا في تلك الشريعة نكاح المرأة بغير بدل تستحقه المرأة

RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r8.claim: That earlier law did not invalidate a marriage contract merely because it contained conditions not required by the contract itself.
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r8.anchor: وعلى أن عقد النكاح لا تفسده الشروط التي لا يوجبها العقد

RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r9.claim: Taʾjurnī can mean that Moses works as the speaker’s hired laborer; alternatively, the verb can mean granting or assigning something to someone.
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r9.anchor: تأجرني من أجرته إذا كنت له أجيرا وثماني حجج ظرفه

RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r10.claim: He parses the eight years as the object and understands the service as tending for eight years.
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r10.anchor: وثماني حجج مفعول به ومعناه رعية ثماني حجج

RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r11.claim: One reading is that the speaker will not impose the more complete of the two terms; a grave demand seems to divide one’s judgment between ability and inability.
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r11.anchor: لا أريد أن أشق عليك بإلزام أثم الرجلين ، فإن قيل ما حقيقة قولهم شققت عليه

RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r12.claim: Alternatively, he promises lenience in the herding work and will not demand extreme care in how Moses tends the flock.
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r12.anchor: لا أريد أن أشق عليك في الرعي ولكني أساهلك فيها وأسامحك بقدر الإمكان

RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r13.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r13.claim: The cited report calls the Prophet an excellent partner who did not act evasively, dishonestly, or quarrelsomely; al-Razi uses it to exemplify gentleness in dealings.
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r13.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شريكي فكان خير شريك لا يداري ولا يشاري ولا يماري

RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r14.claim: The promised righteousness may mean good dealings and a gentle manner, or righteousness generally, which includes good dealings.
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r14.anchor: الأول : يريد بالصلاح حسن المعاملة ولين الجانب والثاني : يريد الصلاح على العموم ويدخل تحته حسن المعاملة

RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r15.claim: The speaker qualifies his promise with God willing because he depends on God’s enabling and assistance.
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r15.anchor: وإنما قال إن شاء الله للاتكال على توفيقه ومعونته

RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p207#2/r16.claim: Asked how the marriage contract can stand with this condition, given that saying “my wife is divorced if God wills” does not effect divorce, al-Razi answers that rulings differ between religious laws.

STUDYQURAN:28:27/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:27/r1.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:28:27/r1.claim: The father means he will be fair and reasonable in his demands during the eight years of service requested for his daughter's hand.
STUDYQURAN:28:27/r1.anchor: he was saying that he would be fair and reasonable in his demands during that period of time (R)

TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r1.claim: The father asks Moses to compensate him for the marriage by tending his flock for eight years; taʾjurnī here means reward or compensate me.
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r1.anchor: على أن تثيبني من تزويجها رعي ماشيتي ثماني حجج، من قول الناس: آجرك الله فهو يأجرك، بمعنى: أثابك الله

TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r2.speaker: بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r2.claim: Some Basran grammarians describe ajartu ghulāmī as the Arabic form meaning I paid my servant, with the passive maʾjūr.
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r2.anchor: حكى بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة أن لغة العرب: أجرت غلامي فهو مأجور، وآجرته فهو مؤجر، يريد: أفعلته

TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r3.claim: Another reported analysis treats ājarah as the reciprocal form fāʿaltu, yielding muʾājir.
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم: آجره فهو مؤاجر، أراد فاعلته

TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says ḥijaj means years and that tending the flock for eight years was the bride’s marriage payment.
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r4.anchor: وكأن أباها عندي جعل صداق ابنته التي زوجها موسى رعي موسى عليه ماشيته ثماني حجج، والحجج: السنون

TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r5.claim: Eight years are the stipulated term; if Moses completes ten, the additional two are a voluntary kindness rather than a marriage condition.
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r5.anchor: فإن أتممت الثماني الحجج عشرا التي شرطتها عليك بإنكاحي إياك إحدى ابنتي، فجعلتها عشر حجج، فإحسان من عندك

TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r6.claim: The father says he does not intend to burden Moses by imposing the full ten years.

TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r7.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r7.claim: Ibn Isḥāq explains the father’s promised righteousness as good companionship and fulfillment of his word.
TAB-FULL:v18p229#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق: " {ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصالحين} [القصص: 27] أي في حسن الصحبة والوفاء بما قلت

TABATABAI:28:22-28/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-28/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:22-28/r8.claim: God answered Moses’ three prayers: he was safe from his pursuers, reached the road to Midian, and received provision through the watering reward, ten years’ livelihood, and a wife.
TABATABAI:28:22-28/r8.anchor: وعند ذلك تمت استجابته تعالى لموسى عليه السلام أدعيته الثلاثة

TABATABAI:28:26-28/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r2.claim: Shuʿayb offered Moses eight or ten years of service in exchange for marrying one daughter; it was not a final contract, since he did not specify which daughter.
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r2.anchor: عرض من شعيب لموسى عليه السلام أن يأجره نفسه ثماني سنين أو عشرا قبال تزويجه

TABATABAI:28:26-28/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r3.claim: The phrase shows that both daughters were present at the time of the offer.

TABATABAI:28:26-28/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r4.claim: Moses was to hire himself out to Shuʿayb for eight حجج; حجة is used for a year because each year includes a pilgrimage to the House.
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r4.anchor: والحجج جمع حجة والمراد بها السنة بعناية أن كل سنة فيها حجة للبيت الحرام

TABATABAI:28:26-28/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r5.claim: The wording indicates that pilgrimage to the House, a rite from Abraham’s law, was practiced by Shuʿayb’s people.
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r5.anchor: وبه يظهر أن حج البيت - وهو من شريعة إبراهيم عليه السلام - كان معمولا به عندهم

TABATABAI:28:26-28/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r6.claim: If Moses completed ten years, the additional two were voluntary and Shuʿayb could not require them.
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r6.anchor: فهو من عندك وباختيار منك من غير أن تكون ملزما من عندي

TABATABAI:28:26-28/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r7.claim: Shuʿayb says the service he seeks is not burdensome and presents himself as a good employer.
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r7.anchor: إخبار عن نحو ما يريده منه من الخدمة وأنه عمل غير موصوف بالمشقة

TABATABAI:28:26-28/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r8.claim: The exception concerns Moses finding Shuʿayb among the righteous, not whether Shuʿayb himself is righteous.
TABATABAI:28:26-28/r8.anchor: فالاستثناء متعلق بوجدان موسى إياه منهم لا بكونه في نفسه منهم

TABATABAI:28:22-28#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-28#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:28:22-28#2/r4.claim: The same report says Moses completed ten years because prophets choose what is most complete and virtuous; al-Qummī relates a similar report.
TABATABAI:28:22-28#2/r4.anchor: فروي أنه قضى أتمهما لأن الأنبياء عليهم السلام لا تأخذ إلا بالفضل والتمام

TABATABAI:28:27/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:27/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:28:27/r4.claim: A report in al-Majmaʿ from Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq identifies the inviting daughter as Moses’ wife, says he completed ten years and married before the term ended, and permits hiring in a marriage arrangement because Moses knew he would live to fulfill it.
TABATABAI:28:27/r4.anchor: قال وسائل أيتهما التي قالت إن أبي يدعوك؟ قال التي تزوج بها

TABATABAI:28:27/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:27/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:28:27/r5.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthūr reports through several routes from the Prophet that Moses completed the full ten years.
TABATABAI:28:27/r5.anchor: وروى قضاء عشر سنين في الدر المنثورعن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بعدة طرق

TABATABAI:28:27/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:27/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:28:27/r6.claim: Asked by al-Ḥalabī whether pilgrimage to the House preceded the Prophet, Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq answered yes, citing Shuʿayb’s use of حجج rather than سنين.
TABATABAI:28:27/r6.anchor: وقال الحلبي سئل أبو عبد الله عليه السلام عن البيت أكان يحج قبل أن يبعث النبي

TABRISI:28:26-27/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:26-27/r2.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:28:26-27/r2.claim: In a noncanonical reading, al-Ḥasan reads al-ajalayni with lightened, vowelless yāʾ.
TABRISI:28:26-27/r2.anchor: قراءة الحسن الأجلين بتخفيف الياء وسكونها

TABRISI:28:26-27/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:26-27/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:26-27/r5.claim: Hātayn qualifies bintay; thamāni ḥijaj is a temporal adverb, and dhalika is a subject with baynī wa-baynak as predicate.
TABRISI:28:26-27/r5.anchor: هاتين صفة لابنتي. ثماني حجج ظرف زمان

TABRISI:28:26-27/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:26-27/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:26-27/r13.claim: Shuʿayb offers one daughter in marriage for eight years of work; completing ten is voluntary generosity, not an obligation.
TABRISI:28:26-27/r13.anchor: أي على أن تكون أجيرا لي ثماني سنين

TABRISI:28:26-27/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:26-27/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:26-27/r14.claim: One view makes the service the marriage payment; another says Shuʿayb paid a dowry and separately hired Moses for shepherding. The latter fits Abū Ḥanīfa’s school, but service-as-dowry better fits the verse’s surface sense.
TABRISI:28:26-27/r14.anchor: وقيل: معناه على أن تجعل جزائي وثوابي إياك

TABRISI:28:26-27/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:26-27/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:26-27/r15.claim: Shuʿayb will not burden Moses with duties beyond tending sheep; alternatively, he will not force Moses to complete ten years.
TABRISI:28:26-27/r15.anchor: في هذه الثمانية حجج وأن أكلفك خدمة سوى رعي الغنم

TABRISI:28:26-27/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:26-27/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:26-27/r16.claim: Shuʿayb conditions his good companionship and fidelity on God’s will because his survival is uncertain and God may take him before he can act rightly.
TABRISI:28:26-27/r16.anchor: إنما علق الصلاح بمشيئة الله لأن مراده

TABRISI:28:26-27/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:26-27/r17.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
TABRISI:28:26-27/r17.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Sallām relates that Moses was allotted each sheep skin set against its mother’s coloring; God then inspired him in a dream to cast his staff into water, after which all lambs bore opposite markings.
TABRISI:28:26-27/r17.anchor: وحكى يحيى بن سلام أنه جعل لموسى كل سلخة

FARRA:v2p304/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p304/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p304/r7.claim: The wage was eight years of tending the sheep; completing ten would be a voluntary gift from Moses.
FARRA:v2p304/r7.anchor: أن تجعل ثوابي أن ترعى علي غنمي ثماني حجج (فإن أتممت عشرا فمن عندك) يقول: فهو تطوع.

THALABI:v7p245/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p245/r3.speaker: شعيب الجبائي
THALABI:v7p245/r3.claim: Shuʿayb al-Jubbaʾi names Moses's wife Safura and her sister Labani.
THALABI:v7p245/r3.anchor: قول شعيب الجبائي قال: امرأة موسى صفورة،

THALABI:v7p245/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p245/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
THALABI:v7p245/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq names the daughters Safura and Sharafa.

THALABI:v7p245/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p245/r5.speaker: غيرهم
THALABI:v7p245/r5.claim: Other authorities say the elder daughter was Safra and the younger Safira.

THALABI:v7p245/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p245/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p245/r6.claim: Taʾjurni means ajirni, ‘hire me’; the verb can also be used of God rewarding someone.
THALABI:v7p245/r6.anchor: قال: [يقول العرب] آجرك الله فهو يأجرك بمعنى أثابك

THALABI:v7p245/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p245/r7.speaker: الأئمة
THALABI:v7p245/r7.claim: The authorities say that tending the father's livestock for eight years was the payment serving as the marriage dowry.
THALABI:v7p245/r7.anchor: قالت الأئمة: على أن تثيبني من تزويجها رعي ماشيتي ثماني حجج

THALABI:v7p245/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p245/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p245/r8.claim: A ḥijja here means a year, and ḥijaj is its plural.

THALABI:v7p245/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p245/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p245/r9.claim: The extra two years are a voluntary favor from Moses, not a condition stipulated in the marriage contract.
THALABI:v7p245/r9.anchor: وأنت به متبرع متفضل وليس مما اشترطه عليك في عقد النكاح

THALABI:v7p245/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p245/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p245/r10.claim: The father promises not to burden Moses and says he will be among the righteous by keeping his agreement and treating him well.
THALABI:v7p245/r10.anchor: ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصالحين من الوافين بالعهد، المحسنين الصحبة

THALABI:v7p245/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p245/r12.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v7p245/r12.claim: Ikrima says Adam brought Moses's staff from Paradise and Gabriel took it after Adam's death, keeping it until he met Moses at night and handed it to him.
THALABI:v7p245/r12.anchor: فقال عكرمة: خرج بها آدم من الجنة وأخذها جبريل بعد موت آدم

THALABI:v7p245/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p245/r13.speaker: آخرون
THALABI:v7p245/r13.claim: Others say prophets inherited the staff until it reached Shuʿayb, who held the prophets' staffs and gave one to Moses.
THALABI:v7p245/r13.anchor: وقال آخرون: لم يزل الأنبياء يتوارثونها حتى وصلت إلى شعيب وكانت عصي الأنبياء عنده

THALABI:v7p245/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p245/r14.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v7p245/r14.claim: Al-Suddi tells how an angel entrusted the staff to Shuʿayb; his daughter repeatedly could take only that staff for Moses, and Shuʿayb later disputed its ownership with Moses and sought an arbitrator.
THALABI:v7p245/r14.anchor: وقال السدي: كانت تلك العصا استودعها ملك

THALABI:v7p246/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p246/r1.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v7p246/r1.claim: In al-Suddi's staff story, an angel arbitrates that whichever man can lift the staff from the ground owns it; Shuʿayb cannot lift it, but Moses can.
THALABI:v7p246/r1.anchor: ضعوها بالأرض فمن حملها فهي له، فعالجها الشيخ فلم يطقها

THALABI:v7p246/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p246/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p246/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas's account says Yathrun had thirteen staffs in a private room; his eleven sons each burned and died after being sent to retrieve one, while Moses took a staff for herding, leading Yathrun to recognize him as a prophet.
THALABI:v7p246/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال: كان في دار يثرون بيت لا يدخله إلا يثرون وابنته

THALABI:v7p246/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p246/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p246/r3.claim: Another story says Shuʿayb sent Moses left at a fork to avoid a dragon, but the sheep went right; while Moses slept, his staff killed the dragon and returned bloody.
THALABI:v7p246/r3.anchor: فإن هناك تنينا عظيما أخشى عليك وعلى الأغنام منه

THALABI:v7p246/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p246/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p246/r4.claim: Moses sees the dead dragon and bloody staff as a sign of God's power; Shuʿayb, who is blind, finds the sheep healthier, then offers Moses that year's piebald young goats as a reward for his herding.
THALABI:v7p246/r4.anchor: فعاد إلى شعيب، وكان شعيب ضريرا فمس الأغنام، فإذا هي أمثل حالا

THALABI:v7p246/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p246/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p246/r5.claim: God tells Moses to strike the water at the flock's watering place.
THALABI:v7p246/r5.anchor: فأوحى الله تعالى إلى موسى أن اضرب بعصاك الماء الذي في مستقى الأغنام

THALABI:v7p246#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p246#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p246#2/r1.claim: Moses strikes the water, and every ewe bears a piebald offspring; Shuʿayb recognizes this as provision from God for Moses and his wife, fulfills his bargain, and hands over the flock.
THALABI:v7p246#2/r1.anchor: فضرب موسى بعصاه الماء ثم سقى الأغنام منه، فما أخطأت واحدة منها إلا وقد

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332#2/r1.claim: Taʾjurnī means to compensate him for the marriage; divine ajr is likewise recompense for a deed.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332#2/r1.anchor: على أن تأجرني} أي تجازيني عن التزويج، والأجر من الله إنما هو: الجزاء على العمل.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r1.claim: The women returned knowing Moses's strength and trustworthiness; when one described him, the father became more interested and offered a daughter in marriage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r1.anchor: فصدرتا وقد عرفتا قوته وأمانته، فلما ذكرت المرأة من حاله بما ذكرت زاده ذلك رغبة فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r2.claim: Unkiḥaka means I will marry her to you.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r2.anchor: أي: أزوجكها {على أن تأجرني ثماني حجج}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r3.claim: The marriage is conditional on Moses working for the father as a hired hand for eight years.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r3.anchor: أي: تكون أجيرا لي ثماني سنين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ understands the stipulated service as making the reward be tending the father's sheep for eight years.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء: يقول أن تجعل ثوابي أن ترعى علي غنمي {ثماني # حجج}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains the service as compensation for the marriage; ajr from God means recompense for work.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r5.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: أي تجازيني من التزويج، والأجر من الله: الجزاء على العمل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r6.claim: Muqātil glosses the phrase as hiring Moses himself for eight years.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل: على أن تأجرني نفسك {ثماني حجج}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r7.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash records Arabic forms for hiring: ajartu with ajr gives maʾjūr, while other forms yield muʾjir or muʾājir.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r7.anchor: قال الأخفش: وهي لغة للعرب؛ منهم من يقول: أجرت (4) غلامي أجرا فهو مأجور

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r8.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r8.claim: Al-Mubarrad distinguishes short ajartu from long ājartu, says the former is more frequent, and distinguishes ijāra as the name from ijār as the verbal noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p376/r8.anchor: وقال المبرد: ويقال: أجرت داري ومملوكي، غير ممدود، وآجرت ممدود

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p377/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p377/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p377/r1.claim: Completing ten years is a voluntary favor from Moses, not an obligation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p377/r1.anchor: أي ذلك تفضل منك ليس بواجب عليك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p377/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p377/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p377/r2.claim: The father does not intend to make Moses work the additional two years as a hardship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p377/r2.anchor: {وما أريد أن أشق عليك} في العشر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p377/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p377/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p377/r3.claim: Muqātil glosses among the righteous as being gentle toward Moses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p377/r3.anchor: {ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصالحين} قال مقاتل:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p377/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p377/r4.speaker: عمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p377/r4.claim: A report from ʿUmar explains the phrase as good companionship and fulfilling what was promised.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p377/r4.anchor: وعن عمر، أي: في حسن الصحبة، والوفاء بما قلت

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:26-28/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:26-28/r3.speaker: الشيخ
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:26-28/r3.claim: The old man offered Moses marriage to one of his two daughters in exchange for eight years of service; completing ten would be voluntary, and he did not wish to burden Moses but promised to keep the agreement.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:26-28/r3.anchor: عند ذلك الشيخ لموسى: { إني أريد أن أنكحك } أزوجك { إحدى ابنتي هاتين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:26-28/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:26-28/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:26-28/r4.claim: The extra two years were not an obligation; the father said he would not impose that burden and would be faithful to the covenant.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:26-28/r4.anchor: وليس بواجب عليك { وما أريد أن أشق عليك } بأن اشترط العشر { ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصالحين } الوافين بالعهد

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p588/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p588/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p588/r1.claim: The father proposes to marry one of his two daughters to Moses on condition that Moses hire out his labor to him.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p588/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p588/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p588/r2.claim: Moses must work eight years, with two further years voluntary if he completes ten; the father promises not to make things hard and to treat him gently.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p588/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p588/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p588/r3.claim: A later agreement gives Moses any lamb born in that pregnancy with a coat unlike its mother's; following God's instruction to put his staff in the filled troughs, all the lambs were born unlike their mothers and Moses took them that year.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p588/r3.anchor: كل سخلة تخرج على غير شبه أمها في هذا البطن فهي لك، فأوحى الله إلى موسى: إذا ملأت الحياض وقربتها لتشرب، فألق عصاك في الحياض

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p588/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p588/r4.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p588/r4.claim: Another version of the bargain gives Moses every spotted lamb born; all the lambs were then born spotted.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p588/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم: كل بلقاء تولد فهي لك، فولدن بلقا كلهن.

MAJAZ:v2p102/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p102/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p102/r2.claim: Taʾjuranī derives from payment for labor: ajartu my worker means I paid him; ajraka Allāh means may God reward you.
MAJAZ:v2p102/r2.anchor: على أن تأجرني ثماني حجج» (27) مجازه من الإجارة وهى أجر العمل يقال: أجرت أجيرى أي أعطيته أجره

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:25/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:25/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:25/r3.claim: At one daughter's suggestion, the parties made the marriage and service agreement described in verse 27.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:25/r3.anchor: kızlardan birinin teklifi üzerine âyette belirtildiği şekilde bir anlaşma yapılmıştır

BURHAN:v3p162/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p162/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p162/r6.claim: In Moses’s prospective employer’s condition, “that you hire me” omits the object “yourself.”
BURHAN:v3p162/r6.anchor: الظاهر أنه متعد حذف مفعوله أي تأجرني نفسك

DAMGHANI:v1p88/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p88/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p88/r4.claim: أتمّ means to finish or complete; Moses completing ten years is an example.
DAMGHANI:v1p88/r4.anchor: الثالث : أتم يعني أكمل . قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

BURHAN:v4p290/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p290/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p290/r7.claim: In the agreement about ten years, min ʿindik means by your favor and generosity.

BURHAN:v3p27/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.claim: Repeated tellings of Moses and Pharaoh differ in wording, order, and detail because each version carries a nuance found only there; unlike earlier scripture's separate single tellings, Joseph's story is collected in one sura.
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.anchor: فقد يوجد في ألفاظها زيادة ونقصان وتقديم وتأخير

DAMGHANI:v1p335/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p335/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p335/r3.claim: Min ʿindik can mean through your favor or generosity.
DAMGHANI:v1p335/r3.anchor: العاشر من عندك اي بفضلك قوله تعالى في سورة القصص فان اتممت عشرا فمن عندك اي بفضلك

DAMGHANI:v1p332/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r8.claim: ʿAlā can introduce a condition: the marriage proposal is conditional on Moses working for the speaker for eight years.
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r8.anchor: على بمعنى الشرط قوله سبحانه في سورة القصص اني اريد ان انكحك احدى ابنتي هاتين على ان تاجرني ثماني حجج

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r7.claim: A third sense is gentleness or kind treatment.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r7.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الصلاح في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1085/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1085/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1085/r1.claim: The yā takes fatḥ obligatorily after a defective noun, in the dual, and in the sound masculine plural; elsewhere both fatḥ and sukūn may occur as transmitted.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1085/r1.anchor: بعد المثنى (رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيَّ (28) نوح) لا بد من الفتح

IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.claim: Of twelve disputed possessive yāʾs, Nafi opens all except معي ردءا, which he leaves quiescent.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.anchor: ففتحهن نافع إلا قوله ﴿ معي ردءا ﴾ فإنه أسكنها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr open nine listed possessive yāʾs and leave quiescent إني أريد, ستجدني إن شاء الله, and معي ردءا.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.anchor: وفتح ابن كثير تسع آيات منهن وأسكن ﴿ إني أريد ﴾ و ﴿ ستجدني إن شاء الله ﴾

NASHR:v2p247/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p247/r11.speaker: ابن كثير
NASHR:v2p247/r11.claim: Ibn Kathir geminates nūn in all five forms; Abu Amr and Ruways agree on فذانك, while the others lighten them. The reading follows Ibn Kathir's treatment of long alif and yāʾ at two sukūns.
NASHR:v2p247/r11.anchor: اللذان، وهذان، وهاتين، فذانك، واللذين في حم السجدة فقرأ ابن كثير بتشديد النون

NASHR:v2p342/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p342/r8.speaker: المدنيان
NASHR:v2p342/r8.claim: The two Medinans open the yāʾ in إني أريد and ستجدني إن شاء الله.
NASHR:v2p342/r8.anchor: إني أريد ستجدني إن شاء الله فتحهما المدنيان
